title: Semantic window regions
summary: Build a desktop-style window from named regions, a title and a body, using the project own CSS. Do not ship bundled icon sprites or third-party font files.
when_to_use: The user wants a dialog or window metaphor and can accept a recreated treatment.
avoid_when: The user needs the operating system native window, or a trademarked system font.

anatomy.purpose: Names the window and holds window controls.
Places the primary and secondary actions.

tokens.name: window.frame
tokens.purpose: Border treatment of the outer frame.

states.name: active
states.behavior: Shows the window as the current dialog.

states.name: inactive
states.behavior: Dims the title treatment without hiding the title text.

responsive: Let the window width follow the viewport up to a readable maximum, instead of a single fixed pixel width.
accessibility: Expose the window as a dialog with an accessible name taken from the title.
Move focus into the window when it opens and return focus when it closes.
implementation_steps: Mark up the frame, title and body as separate regions.
Recreate the border and title treatment with project-owned CSS or theme values.
Do not copy bundled font files or icon sprites; use a licensed font and text or icons the user already has.
Wire focus and the accessible name in the user stack.

source_refs.license_scope: MIT documentation only; bundled font files and icon sprites were not retained
